advice: Propose one distinct tile-mapping experiment: swap the ownership of ZA1 and ZA2 in both full512 K loops. ZA0 and ZA3 keep the top-left and bottom-right quadrants. Route the top-right FMOPA updates to ZA2 and the bottom-left updates to ZA1, then swap their extraction and stores so each result returns to its original C quadrant. Keep all four FP32 accumulators, operands, predicates, K order, loop schedule, and tail fallback unchanged. This is an unverified test of whether changing the cross-quadrant tile assignment affects instruction scheduling. Check fresh-input correctness, input preservation, full output overwrite and guards, general shapes and tails, n<=0, plus the deterministic cancellation and scale-separated cases at n=512 before timing. If correct, use the existing ten-run paired-control gate and unchanged power settings.
risks: The mapping still uses exactly four ZA.S tiles; it does not assume eight FP32 accumulators. This only permutes the two off-diagonal outputs, so it may compile to equivalent machine behavior and has no evidence-based reason to improve speed. Preserve both output destinations exactly. No performance or correctness result for this proposed change is supplied.
